item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because its FilesService.Upload implementation follows the required repository pattern: validate, build the replayable multipart body with multipartbody.NewFile, and delegate to FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B routes Upload through Add, preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics; A duplicates all of that via Raw.Do in direct conflict with the frozen contract.","B’s retry test explicitly enables RetryAllMethods and uses a reader whose concrete type is not one net/http automatically replays, closely matching the reported failure mode.","A introduces duplicate request machinery and documentation coupled to transport implementation details, increasing drift risk.","B’s core Upload implementation is compact, idiomatic, and directly reuses established behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add, violating an explicit architectural requirement and duplicating its behavior.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods: true, so it does not directly reproduce the user’s stated configuration.","No added tests visibly cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors."],"risks_b":["The unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and its tests violate scope discipline and the requirement to add exactly the specified convenience API; they should be removed before merge.","The multipart test checks field and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.","No added tests visibly cover validation or source-reader errors."]}
